title: Feasibility indicator over a fixed set: Real Stability
abstract: If a projector fixes feasible points and the closed $\varepsilon$-ball about $x$ lies in the feasible set, then every $x'$ in the ball is fixed. This is an identity certificate, not full Euclidean projection nonexpansiveness. Lean \texttt{LEAN\_FULL}.
problem: \leanpath{feasibility-indicator} is treated via a feasibility indicator / projection that fixes InSet points.
intuition: Deep inside the feasible set, projection is the identity, so small moves stay fixed points.
proof: Take $|x'-x|\le\varepsilon$. Feasibility of the ball gives $\mathrm{InSet}(x')$ and $\mathrm{InSet}(x)$. Fixing feasible points yields $\mathrm{proj}(x')=x'$ and $\mathrm{proj}(x)=x$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:inv}). Sharpness is the contrapositive of ball feasibility. \textbf{Limitation:} this does not prove general Euclidean projection nonexpansiveness.
consequences: Honest limited certificate for simplex/$\ell_p$-ball style operators in this library. Related: projection-interval, coordinate-clipping.
